einzeiler: Scott Jennings analyzes the latest economic data, wildfire strategy, and politics.
kurzfassung: Scott Jennings covers the US jobs report, health insurance costs, and political strategy for the upcoming midterms. The episode features interviews with U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach on new currency and wildland fire chief Brian Fennessy on agency unification. Additionally, Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller discusses the 25th anniversary of 9/11, and Jennings broadcasts his speech from the Republican Jewish Coalition.
stichpunkte: U.S. non-farm payrolls for August increase by 162,000 jobs, with unemployment holding at 4.1 percent.
A new survey projects health benefit costs to rise over 8 percent next year, driven by rising expenses.
Pollster John McLaughlin advises Republicans to frame the midterm elections around competing economic systems.
U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach discusses new circulating coins honoring America's 250th anniversary and the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
Brian Fennessy outlines the unification of Department of the Interior wildland fire agencies to improve emergency response.
Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller discusses the upcoming White House ceremony featuring a steel beam from the South Tower.
Scott Jennings delivers his full speech at the Republican Jewish Coalition in Las Vegas, emphasizing Judeo-Christian values.

kapitel.titel: Lindsey Clancy Trial Update and Legal Analysis
Interview with U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach
Wildfire Strategy and U.S. Wildland Fire Service
Interview with Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller
Speech at the Republican Jewish Coalition

beschreibung:
On today’s edition of The Scott Jennings Show, Scott broadcasts from New York with a look at the stronger-than-expected August jobs report, rising healthcare costs and the economic argument Republicans could take to voters in the midterms, while also covering a First Amendment victory for independent journalists in Washington state and the mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder case. Republican congressional nominee Ralph Alvarado joins Scott to discuss Kentucky’s 6th District race, healthcare, affordability, public safety and President Trump’s agenda, while U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach weighs in on the jobs numbers, fiscal discipline and a new $1 coin commemorating America’s 250th anniversary. U.S. Wildland Fire Service Director Brian Fennessy discusses preparations for peak wildfire season, prevention and the government’s new approach to protecting communities, and Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller looks ahead to the 25th anniversary of 9/11, shares the story of his brother FDNY firefighter Stephen Siller and discusses his new memoir, Let Us Do Good. The program closes with a special presentation of Scott’s speech to the Republican Jewish Coalition in Las Vegas.
